newsitem.title: GERMANY: Wall St, M3 fuels correction on German share mkt.
newsitem.headline: Wall St, M3 fuels correction on German share mkt.

text.p: Signs of the long-expected correction emerged on the German share market on Thursday as prices dropped sharply in early bourse trade, extending a fall begun in late trading on Wednesday.

A weak performance on Wall Street weighed on the market and jitters ahead of Friday's triple witching options expiry added to volatility, but dealers said the feeling on the market was that prices had been pushed up to unrealistic levels.
"We haven't had really negative numbers but I suppose people are thinking now that it can't get better than this. And we really need to clear the air here," said a Frankfurt dealer.
The DAX index was down 42.64 points, or 1.3 percent, at 3,191.11 points in early trade. Declines had set in late the previous day after a wave of selling on U.S. markets.

A larger than expected rise in German January M3 money supply data on Thursday briefly added to pressure on the market, although the effect was shortlived as economists said this would not motivate a German interest rate hike.

Insurer Allianz AG Holding was among the main decliners, down 65 marks at 3,175 marks. The insurer is being hit by profit-taking after announcing a double digit rise in earnings for 1996, broadly in line with expectations.
Engineering group Mannesmann AG was more stable, down 3.50 marks at 674.50 marks after announcing a doubling of its telecommunications earnings and plans to raise its dividend by one mark.
Although some dealers said the dividend hike was less than had been expected, Mannesmann's overall message was neutral to positive.

Siemens AG dropped 1.20 marks to 84.60 marks despite a projection that its semi-conductors division would triple sales by the year 2001. Dealers said the market was pessimistic on the division in general, whose profits fell to 603 million marks in the 1995/1996 business year from 793 million.
